record.description: bptIn, s, p and every abort amount are whole balanceOf(this) values rather than deltas. A stray non-proportional sUSDS/phUSD transfer to the escrow shifts the seeded price. Mitigations were found: the recipient is pinned (LP goes to newPooler, abort goes to oldPooler), and the donor loses money. Seeding (S, P+x) and arbitraging back to the true price yields at most (sqrt(P+x)-sqrt(S))^2, which is less than x for S≈P. Not exploitable for profit. The remaining value of this record is the price-shift note, which feeds PATTERN-003.
presentMitigations: recipient pinned to a non-caller address

record.description: _bpt is snapshotted from oldPooler.pool(), but BalancerPoolerV2.setPool is owner-mutable and withdrawBPT pays IERC20(_pool) (the CURRENT pool). If setPool runs between escrow deploy and withdrawBPT, and oldPooler holds the new pool's BPT, then the escrow receives a token it can neither exit (NoBPT) nor abort. The escrow has no generic rescue, so that token is stranded forever. Would a competent owner be surprised by this? Plausibly yes (Law 3 footgun), though the precondition is unlikely.

record.description: The escrow has no rescue for tokens outside {BPT, sUSDS, phUSD, USDS}, no receive or fallback, and no key fallback: all three functions are onlyOperator, and operator is immutable. Losing the operator key strands all four balances, which story-052 accepts by design (Law 3). Any other token sent here, including a wrong BPT (MR-002), is lost permanently. The story rates this INFO (L323, L345).

record.description: IERC4626(_sUSDS).deposit(amt, _newPooler) has no minimum-shares check. The run found this NOT vulnerable in practice: the sUSDS share price comes from the Sky chi accumulator and not from balanceOf, so donations cannot manipulate it, and sUSDS has a very large existing supply. record.description: skim(_newPooler) sends any unsynced phUSD donation to UniPoolerV2. UniPoolerV2.pool() never consumes phUSD it holds, so the phUSD can only be recovered through the owner's rescueERC20, which story-052 L129 accepts. PairSkimmed emits the pre-skim pair BALANCES (b0, b1), not the skimmed excess. Those are equal only because reserves are (0,0) at that point, so the event is correct as written but fragile.

record.description: The L-21 fix guard `if (address(hook) == _defaultHook) revert HookNotSet()` (L356; _defaultHook captured at L230) blocks only the one DefaultDispatchHook instance deployed by the base constructor. A different no-op hook (for example a second DefaultDispatchHook, or a stale hook redeployed by a script) passes the guard and recreates the L-21 zero-mint-debt outcome. setHook rejects only address(0) (ATokenDispatcherV2 L95). A mint-debt hook whose `dispatcher` is not repointed to UniPoolerV2 fails loudly in onDispatch (dispatcher-gated), which is safe. Reaching the bypass needs an owner/script action, so this is a residual Law-3 footgun, not an attacker path. The fix covers the failure mode L-21 states (setHook skipped or reordered).

record.failLoudNote: NFTMinterV2.mint calls dispatcher.dispatch at L191 with no try/catch, so until setHook runs, every index-4 mint reverts UniPoolerV2__HookNotSet. The other indices are unaffected. This is an intended fail-loud ordering requirement (NatSpec 'Hook must be set before the first mint'), not a DoS finding, provided the cutover script calls setHook before registering index 4.

record.description: quotePool reads totalSupply() (L517) without the _mintFee LP that pair.mint() issues to feeTo when the V2 fee switch is on. Fees accrued since kLast, plus any donation folded in by sync(), grow sqrt(k). In execution, the pooler's liquidity is computed against a larger totalSupply, so the realised LP is at least the quote. The divergence errs in the safe direction for a minLP derived from quotePool. The quote's swapIn and phusdOut match pool() exactly after sync. The real exposure is TOCTOU: the keeper derives minPhusdOut/minLP off-chain from quotePool and executes in a later block (already the L-22/L-23 tolerance surface). If the keeper is ever a contract that calls quotePool in the same transaction, the mins become vacuous. No such caller exists in the source.

record.description: The canonical check takes its factory from the caller-supplied router_ (IUniswapV2Router02(router_).factory()). A wrong router plus a matching fake factory would pass. Router and pair are both deploy-time owner/deployer inputs, so this is Law-3 trusted (an obvious misconfig) unless the deploy script reads the router from an unverified source. The check also needs the pair to exist before deployment (getPair returns 0 and pair_ != 0), which pushes pair creation and seeding into the L-24 pre-seed window.
